reasoning: The PKGBUILD downloads from official sources (registry.npmjs.org with sha512sums, nodejs.org for CachyOS fallback) with no evidence of malicious injection. The CachyOS Node.js fallback is a transparent workaround from the official Node.js distribution site, not a supply-chain risk. All executable logic is contained in package() with --ignore-scripts preventing upstream post-install hooks. No top-level code execution, no fetching from unrelated hosts, no obfuscation.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is artifactual, not substantive. Qwen returned 'inconclusive' due to an HTTP 400 API error when reviewing .SRCINFO, not due to security concerns. Openrouter/free (advisory-only, doesn't count as a vote) had a parse error on LICENSE. Deepseek correctly reviewed all files and returned 'safe'. All models that successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD agreed it contains standard AUR practices with no malicious behavior.
coverage_issues: Qwen: .SRCINFO review failed with HTTP 400 API error, causing inconclusive verdict despite PKGBUILD being safe
Openrouter/free: LICENSE review failed with parse error, causing inconclusive verdict
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parse errors) should not produce 'inconclusive' security verdicts when the actual security-relevant files were successfully reviewed and found safe. The audit system should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool error' and 'inconclusive due to genuine security uncertainty'.

Models correctly identified the CachyOS Node.js fallback pattern as legitimate. This pattern (downloading from official upstream without checksum pinning for build-time workarounds) should be documented as a known-safe pattern to prevent future false positives.
When multiple models agree on 'safe' for the PKGBUILD (the primary attack surface), tool errors on metadata files (.SRCINFO, LICENSE) should not override the substantive security analysis.
